title: A weighted value from fixed references and swing ratings

blocks.text: The practice utility's board scores its projects on three measures instead of GridCap's two: NPV ($k), risk removed ($k) and customer-minutes of outage avoided. You receive one table per measure, keyed `(project id, start year)` like every coefficient table of milestone 3, and must fold them into one value per start that the model can maximize.

The board has fixed, before any project was scored, a **reference** $`R_k`$ for each measure (the swing from no benefit to this much, in the measure's own unit) and a **swing rating** $`s_k`$ for each (the biggest swing gets 100). The weights and the value are

so $`m/R`$ has no unit, zero means no benefit, and a project's value does not depend on which other projects are candidates (lessons 7.4.2 and 7.4.3). Restating a measure in other units together with its reference must change nothing (lesson 7.4.4).

items: `value_table(measures, reference=REFERENCE, ratings=RATINGS)`: `{(i, t): v}` over every key found in any measure's table (a missing entry counts as 0), each value rounded to 6 decimals. Use the `reference` it is given.
`ranking(table)`: every key, highest value first; equal values in key order, so two runs always list them the same way.

cases.says: every start gets one value, a start with no benefit in any measure is worth 0, and the ranking lists every start from the highest value down
the weights are the swing ratings divided by their total, so they sum to 1
the whole value table matches the reference, each measure divided by its fixed reference
withdrawing a project changes no other project's value, because the references do not come from the candidates
restating risk in $M together with its reference leaves every value and the ranking unchanged
starts of equal value are ranked by their key, so the ranking is the same in every run
